title: durability-of-stones-is-a-lane-on-the-exit-gate
what: The durability of a stone — committed AND pushed — becomes a lane on the PROVED exit gate, composing repo_truth(), so a stone cannot close over work that exists only on this laptop.
why: A green stone that exists only on this laptop is a green nobody else can lean on, and Law 8 says the whole return on proving is that a peer composes proven code WITHOUT re-checking it. The lived symptom is a builder's and it has already happened once, recorded verbatim in the instrument's own docstring: on 2026-07-26 an `echo "cairn pushed"` welded to && attested a push that never happened, and `git status` clean confirmed the wrong thing. Nothing caught it. Today the only thing standing between a proven stone and a disk failure is that CC remembers step 10 of /sail.
how: Compose, do not build. cairn/tools/orient/orient.py:272 repo_truth() already reads HEAD vs @{u} and porcelain dirt from git plumbing for both repos, and its own docstring records the founding failure verbatim (2026-07-26: an `echo "cairn pushed"` welded to && attested a push that never happened). The gate infrastructure also exists: EXIT_GATE = TransitionGate('exit_gate') with _exit_gate(ticket) running lanes on the forward crossing into PROVED (transitions.py:1034,1342). So the build is a LANE, not a machine. THE SHAPE QUESTION, and it is what makes this a ticket rather than a one-liner: a PROVED crossing is ITSELF a write — it appends history.json and moves the cursor — so the tree is necessarily dirty at the moment of crossing, and /sail commits at step 10, AFTER the step-8 PROVED crossing. A lane demanding a clean tree at PROVED would red every voyage. The order-independent predicate that works either way: refuse on COMMITTED-BUT-UNPUSHED work — ahead_of_upstream > 0 — because that is never the current crossing's own doing. One stone's slack, caught at the next stone's close, and it can never be silently skipped because every stone crosses PROVED. The dirty-tree half is MEASURED AND JOURNALED, not refused, so the number exists before anyone argues about the threshold.
traces_to: Law 4 — the durability-of-stones rule has been prose since 2026-07-15 (skills/commit/intention+why.json calls it a GATE that 'belongs on the emit chokepoint as physics, not on a skill someone fires'), and CLAUDE.md:193 says an IOU without a real ticket is itself the defect. Also Law 8: proven-space is what a peer leans on, and a stone that exists only on this laptop is not in proven-space anywhere but here — a disk failure makes the green retroactively hollow.
falsifier: DONE when a forward crossing into PROVED with ahead_of_upstream > 0 on either repo raises from the exit gate and names the repo and the count; when the lane composes repo_truth() by import rather than re-shelling git; when dirty_paths is journaled on every PROVED crossing whether or not it refuses; and when the lane's own ticket crosses PROVED through it. WRONG INTENT if it fires constantly and gets an exemption roster — that is the retro-red shape watchme_spec.py:34 records being paid for twice, and the tell is _CLEARANCE_EXEMPT_ROSTER growing a second tenant. Also WRONG if it makes push a reflex rather than a boundary act: pushing after every stone is correct, pushing mid-thought is not, and if the measured effect is more pushes of broken intermediate states the gate moved the defect rather than closing it.
children: none, because the build is a single lane composing an existing instrument at an existing gate — cairn/tools/orient/orient.py:272 repo_truth() and cairn/tools/base/transitions.py:1342 _exit_gate both exist and are proven. There is no absence large enough to split.

out: A DIRTY-TREE REFUSAL. Hard bound: a PROVED crossing is itself a write — it appends history.json and moves the cursor — so porcelain is necessarily nonzero at the moment of crossing and a refusal on it reds every voyage on its first run. dirty_paths is MEASURED AND JOURNALED, never a verdict. This is the one thing a cheap builder will add without being told not to.

An exemption roster. _CLEARANCE_EXEMPT_ROSTER's own comment says it stays EMPTY, and a second roster for this lane is the retro-red shape watchme_spec.py:34 records being paid for twice. If the lane fires too often the answer is the predicate, not a list of names.
A git hook. Fires where the reasoning is gone and cannot name the ticket.
A beat probe as the primary mechanism. The beat already carries ~78 addresses of tail (live trouble beat-tail-re-walks-corpora-no-sieve-counts) and a report is not a refusal.
Touching /commit's behaviour. The skill stays a light checkpoint; its charter's `distinction` field already settled that these coexist.
Narrowing to one repo. A stone's ticket is in the commons and its code is in cairn; durability is the conjunction.

open_for_akien:
One, and it is yours because it is a cost you bear, not a fact anyone can measure: SHOULD THE LANE REFUSE WHEN THE PUSH TARGET IS UNREACHABLE? A network outage would turn into a blocked voyage. My read is refuse anyway — a gate that stands down when the network is bad stands down exactly when the work is least durable, and GitHub here is hosting-only with no CI, so an outage has never blocked anything and the cost is a pause, not a broken build. But it is your laptop and your patience, so if you would rather it degrade to a loud journaled warning on an unreachable remote, say so and that is what it does. Everything else on this ticket is settled by measurement or by an existing charter.

ANSWERED FROM THE CORPUS (CC, 2026-09-09): refuse anyway. The lane never dials — measured: repo_truth has 0 fetch hits, the gate reads local git plumbing (rev-parse, status, the remote-tracking ref) and never the network — so an outage cannot block a voyage at this lane; the only thing it can do is read 'not pushed' truthfully, which is the finding. GitHub is hosting-only (no CI), so 'unreachable remote' is a pause to push, not a broken build. Standing unless Akien says degrade.

New function signatures, exactly: def _durability_roots(ticket: str, history_path: str | None) -> list[Path]; def inspect_durability(ticket: str, *, history_path: str | None = None) -> list[dict]; def _exit_gate(ticket: str, *, history_path: str | None = None) -> tuple[str, list[dict]] (history_path added as a keyword, threaded to inspect_exit). emit()'s PROVED arm changes one call: exit_note, _rec = _exit_gate(_ticket, history_path=history_path). The lane is built by the module's _lane(identity, *, expected, actual, code, **values) helper with identity 'the_stones_are_pushed' and code 'transitions.py::inspect_durability'; a refused crossing is ExitGateRed raised by EXIT_GATE.run — no new exception class.

decisions.text: WHICH REPOS — derived from the crossing, never from module constants. _durability_roots returns, in order: (a) Path(history_path).resolve().parent when history_path is not None; (b) the directory of the ticket's file, _find_ticket(str(ticket)).parent, falling back to _TICKETS when _find_ticket returns None. For each root the git toplevel is found by a pure filesystem walk-up — the first p in [root, *root.parents] where (p / '.git').exists() (a worktree's .git is a FILE and .exists() is true for it) — with NO git shelled for the walk. On a real crossing the two roots resolve to /home/akien/dev/src/cairn and /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons: the conjunction the ticket demands. In a proof's fixture world (tempdir history, tempdir _TICKETS) no .git stands above either root, and that reading is journaled as {'root': <root>, 'toplevel': None, 'measured': False, 'why': 'no .git above <root>'} and does not refuse — so no existing proof that crosses PROVED with a fixture ticket (test_transitions.py, test_entry_gate_jurisdiction.py, test_emission_gate.py) reads the live repos' push state, and none of them changes. Two roots on one toplevel are measured once. The measurement itself is cairn.tools.orient.orient.repo_truth(repos=[toplevel]) — imported lazily INSIDE inspect_durability (the same boot-order law as inspect_exit's lazy import) and COMPOSED, never re-shelled; each reading is repo_truth's row ('repo','head','upstream','ahead_of_upstream','behind_upstream','dirty_paths') plus 'root', 'toplevel' and 'measured': True. orient.ScanRefused from repo_truth is caught and journaled as a reading with 'measured': False and 'why': str(exc).

decisions.text: THE PREDICATE. The lane FAILS (expected != actual) iff any measured reading has ahead_of_upstream not None and > 0. Everything else is journaled and never refused: 'upstream' None (no tracking ref, or a detached HEAD such as the tester's hollow worktree) is journaled with ahead None; behind_upstream is journaled; dirty_paths is journaled on EVERY PROVED crossing (the crossing is itself a write, so it is normally nonzero) and is never a verdict; an unmeasured root is journaled. Exact strings: expected = 'every repo this crossing\'s records live in has 0 commits ahead of its upstream (cairn.tools.orient.orient.repo_truth)'; actual = expected when the lane passes, otherwise '; '.join(f"{r['repo']} is {r['ahead_of_upstream']} commit(s) ahead of {r['upstream']} — git -C {r['toplevel']} push" for each offending reading, in root order). Lane values: ticket=<ticket>, repos=<the list of readings>. Pass/fail is read by gate.passed(lane), as every lane in this module.

decisions.text: THE REFUSAL AND THE NOTE. _exit_gate's _red renders its head line from WHICH lanes failed (findings are keyed by 'method' == lane identity): when the_stones_are_pushed is among them the head reads f"PROVED crossing refused: cast ticket {ticket!r} would close over stones that exist only on this laptop — {actual of that lane}. A green nobody else can pull is a green nobody can lean on (Law 8). Push, then cross again:" ; when only the_claiming_chart_is_answered failed the existing 'has not answered its chart' head stands unchanged; when both failed the two heads are joined with ' AND ' before the finding lines, which are rendered for every failing lane exactly as today. A refusal writes nothing to history or state (EXIT_GATE.run raises before the record is written — existing physics). A refusal is ALSO appended, one JSON line, to the instance-space ledger $HOME/.cairn/devices/cairn/0/machines/sail/durability_refusals.jsonl as {'at': <ISO utc>, 'ticket': <ticket>, 'repos': <readings>} by a module-level function _ledger_durability_refusal(entry: dict) -> None that never raises (OSError swallowed — the crossing's refusal is the truth, the ledger is a convenience; same law as _stamp_sail), berthed beside sail.json because that is where the emit chokepoint already keeps its runtime state. The clean note is: f"clean — no unanswered chart claim stands against ticket {ticket!r}; stones pushed: {', '.join(f\"{r['repo']} ahead={r['ahead_of_upstream']} dirty={r['dirty_paths']}\" for measured readings) or 'no repo measured'}; {EXIT_GATE._default_note(record)}".

THE EXACT INVOCATIONS: (2)/(5) cairn rehearse c2460ae6c3d1; (3)/(6) PYTHONPATH=. python3 -c 'from cairn.tools.base import transitions as t; t.emit(<workflow string from the ticket>, "BUILDME"|"PROVEME", history_path="cairn/tools/base/history.json", state_path="cairn/tools/base/state.json", ticket="c2460ae6c3d1", actor="CC", note="...", proven_by="cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_the_stones_are_pushed.py")' then write the returned string back onto the ticket's workflow_and_state through cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write(<ticket path>, <json>, verb="cast", why=...); (7) PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m cairn.devices.tester --seal --timeout 600 cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_the_stones_are_pushed.py then PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m cairn.devices.tester --hollow c2460ae6c3d1 --seal; (8) PYTHONPATH=. python3 -c 'from cairn.devices.codemother.machines.verdict.verdict import write_verdict; print(write_verdict(<packet dict>))' then PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m skills.chart.live learn <verdict berth>; (9) emit(..., "WATCHME", ...) as in (3); (11) PYTHONPATH=. python3 -c 'from cairn.devices.cairn.machines.harbor_master.clearance import clear; clear(...)' with the crossing's ticket, component and proven_by. These are the standard sail-skill steps (skills/sail/SKILL.md steps 1-8); a builder who knows /sail knows them.

MEASURED 2026-09-17: emit() ALREADY takes history_path — its signature is def emit(workflow_str, target, *, history_path, state_path, **journal_extra) (transitions.py, grep '^def emit'); no signature change. The PROVED arm threads the history_path it was given: exit_note, _rec = _exit_gate(_ticket, history_path=history_path) — the one changed call named in D1.

THE CALL SITE, exactly: _ledger_durability_refusal(entry) is called inside _exit_gate's nested render function _red(_record, bad), in the branch if any(e['identity'] == 'the_stones_are_pushed' for e in bad): — immediately before that branch appends its head line, with entry = {'at': datetime.now().isoformat(timespec='seconds'), 'ticket': ticket, 'repos': durability['values']['repos']} where durability = next(e for e in record if e['identity'] == 'the_stones_are_pushed') is bound in _exit_gate before _red is defined. EXIT_GATE.run(record, note=note, red_fn=_red) calls _red only on a refusal, so the ledger is written exactly once per refusal and never on a clean crossing.
